cand.title: Diagnosis and Management of Temporomandibular Disorders
cand.organizationName: University of Toronto Continuing Dental Education

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Two verified organizer-side relationship candidates: Kyle Tran, Senior Program Officer, Continuing Dental Education, whose official biography includes program budgeting, administration and events experience; and Dr. Chris Swayze, Director, Continuing Dental Education. Prioritize Kyle for operational qualification and Chris for programme-level sponsorship. Neither is publicly identified as the hotel contract signatory or this course’s housing buyer. The three advertised instructors are academic faculty, not evidenced lodging buyers.
findings.futureEdition: Officially announced January 22–23, 2027, 8:30 a.m.–4:00 p.m. each day, at Chestnut Conference Centre, 89 Chestnut Street, Toronto, Ontario, Canada. These are course activity dates, not publication dates; both the course page and 2026–2027 schedule agree. This is the next announced edition found within the requested horizon. No later Toronto edition through June 2028 was located; do not infer a 2028 date.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied Radisson product constraints: a downtown city-hotel role is more relevant than a resort proposition for this two-day lecture/hands-on course. Conditional speaker or out-of-town attendee lodging could suit a 157-room hotel, but no attendee count, nonlocal share, peak rooms or room nights is published, so even a 15-room block is not supported. Do not pitch a full-house booking or assume demand reaches the hotel’s 15–109-room target. January teaching and included lunch are assigned elsewhere. Any future classroom proposal must first fit the supplied approximately 240-theatre maximum and hands-on layout; catering availability must be verified independently.
findings.venueCommitments: Both January 2027 teaching days are explicitly scheduled at Chestnut Conference Centre, 89 Chestnut Street. This is downtown Toronto proper, not Harbourfront, MTCC or Exhibition Place. The university conference venue is the published incumbent; its official site now uses The Conference Centre at the University of Toronto. This is a public venue assignment, not inspection of a signed contract. Coffee/tea, lunch and hands-on materials are included in course registration; no separate hotel catering requirement is advertised.
findings.historicalRotation: Published edition schedules: January 26–27, 2024 at 89 Chestnut Street; October 4–5, 2024 at Royal Canadian Military Institute, 426 University Avenue; February 28–March 1, 2025 at Chestnut Conference Centre; January 23–24, 2026 at Chestnut Conference Centre; next announced January 22–23, 2027 at Chestnut Conference Centre. Evidence shows repeat Toronto delivery and one intra-city venue change, not destination rotation or a guaranteed annual cycle. Historical pages document scheduled editions, not audited attendance or proof each course ran.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Unknown for this edition: no edition-specific housing bureau, host lodging hotel, room block, booking code or open hotel RFP was found in the official course and linked accommodation information. The linked general page says: “If you are travelling from out of town and require accommodation, the following hotels are close to our course locations.” It names every hotel as follows: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Toronto Downtown, 108 Chestnut St; Marriott Downtown at CF Toronto Eaton Centre, 525 Bay St; Sheraton Centre Toronto Hotel, 123 Queen St W. This is a proximity list, not evidence of reserved inventory, negotiated rates or exclusivity. Individual booking is plausible but unverified. Chestnut Residence advertises public bookings May–August; do not assume January lodging at the teaching venue.
findings.organizationStructure: The organizer is Continuing Dental Education within the University of Toronto Faculty of Dentistry: a university education unit, not an association, corporate event agency, PCO or DMC. Chestnut is the published teaching venue, not the event owner. No external PCO/DMC or housing intermediary is identified in the reviewed course materials.
findings.competitiveLimitations: The January teaching venue is already published and meals are included. The three hotels on the general accommodation list are competitive referral alternatives, not verified contracted incumbents. Their published addresses are in the course-location district, whereas the supplied Radisson location is Harbourfront; convenience is a potential disadvantage, not a measured travel-time claim. No sold-out notice, contracted room demand, compression or overflow evidence was found. The venue’s public capacity is not course attendance.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Contact Kyle Tran through cde@dentistry.utoronto.ca or 416-864-8100, asking for the January 2027 logistics lead. Qualify nonlocal registrations, speaker accommodation, existing hotel arrangements and whether an additional hotel referral is welcome before sending a rate proposal. Escalate programme partnership discussions to Dr. Chris Swayze at his published chris.swayze@dentistry.utoronto.ca or 416-864-8101. Ask when the next TMD edition and venue decision will be made. Do not present a catering proposal for the committed January teaching days or reserve a speculative room block.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: January 2027 is confirmed upcoming as of November 16, 2026, but it is not an evidenced open venue/catering opportunity. An accommodation referral or speaker-stay approach is possible only after confirming nonlocal demand and whether an existing arrangement exists. Public silence does not establish open hotel sourcing.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: repeated Toronto editions and the October 2024 change to Royal Canadian Military Institute justify a programme relationship and a question about venue-selection timing; they do not establish that the next cycle is competitively available. No post-January-2027 edition or RFP was found. Offer future accommodation referrals first; pursue teaching space only if CDE confirms external venues are considered, attendance/layout fit and catering feasibility.
